images.title: Ten of each makes the next
images.purpose: Shows the Egyptian landmarks 1, 10, 100, 1000, each one 10 times the one before.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A row of four Egyptian symbols from left to right with an arrow between each pair and the value under each.
images.exact_structure: Left to right, four dark outlined symbols in teal (#0072B2), evenly spaced: a single vertical stroke; a heel shaped like an upside down U; a coil of rope shaped like a flat spiral; a lotus flower on a short stem. Under each symbol its value: 1, 10, 100, 1000. Between each pair, one amber (#E69F00) arrow labelled × 10, exactly 3 arrows. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each Egyptian landmark is ten of the one before, so the landmarks are powers of 10.
images.description: Shows the Egyptian landmarks 1, 10, 100, 1000, each one 10 times the one before.
images.context: Worked example writes 2153 as 2 lotuses, 1 coil, 5 heels, 3 strokes; stroke 1, heel 10, coil 100, lotus 1000.

image_decisions.why: The chain of symbols with × 10 arrows shows the building rule of the landmarks in one line.
